problem:
The position $s(t)$ of a particle (in miles) at time $t$ hours is given by 

$$
s(t)=\frac{3}{t},\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the speed of the particle when $t=3\,\text{h}.$

feedback.problem:
The position $s(t)$ of a particle (in centimeters) at time $t$ minutes is given by 

$$
s(t)=3{t}^{6}-2{t}^{4}-8{t}^{2}-7t,\,t\ge 0.
$$

Calculate the speed of the particle when $t=1\,\text{min}.$

The speed of the particle is 
{{field-1}}$\text{cm/min}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{6}-2{t}^{4}-8{t}^{2}-7t) \\  & =18{t}^{5}-8{t}^{3}-16t-7\end{aligned}
$$

When $t=1,$ the velocity is

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =18(1)^{5}-8(1)^{3}-16(1)-7 \\  & =18-8-16-7 \\  & =-13.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the speed is $|-13|=13\,\text{cm/min}.$
